inputs.original_text: Phoenix city leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. Whatever justification they offer, this puts political agendas ahead of cooperation with those charged with enforcing the law. When local officials weaken the ability of federal authorities to do their jobs, public order and community safety are the ones at risk.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix leaders voted Wednesday night to tighten restrictions on ICE and other law enforcement agencies using city property. That’s a necessary step toward making public spaces accountable to the people who live in them, rather than automatically available to federal enforcement. Calling this a threat to safety ignores how aggressive enforcement can put immigrant communities and other vulnerable residents at risk. Community safety means protecting people’s rights and trust, not treating cooperation with law enforcement as an end in itself.
